game_mammals: No Alabama statute or ADCNR rule found that specifically authorizes or regulates salvage of vehicle-killed deer or other game. Ala. Admin. Code r. 220-2-.24 makes it unlawful to possess any freshly killed bird or animal protected by law except during the open season for that species; secondary sources read this as allowing a vehicle-killed deer to be kept during open deer season without a permit.
game_birds: No specific roadkill provision for turkey or upland birds; same open-season possession rule (220-2-.24) would apply. Migratory birds (waterfowl, doves) cannot be possessed without a federal permit under the Migratory Bird Treaty Act.
permit_process: No permit or salvage tag program found. Contacting a local ADCNR Conservation Enforcement Officer before keeping an animal is the prudent course.
timing: No reporting deadline found. Possession of freshly killed protected game appears lawful only during that species' open season.
excluded_species: Protected nongame, state or federally listed species, and MBTA birds. Out-of-season protected game (per 220-2-.24).
sale_of_parts: Not authorized; general prohibitions on selling game apply.
other_restrictions: Alabama has CWD carcass import and transport restrictions; check current ADCNR CWD rules.
statute_or_reg: Ala. Admin. Code r. 220-2-.24 (general possession rule; not roadkill-specific)
agency: Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, Division of Wildlife and Freshwater Fisheries
notes: No official ADCNR roadkill guidance located. Secondary sources (LegalClarity, FreeRangeAmerican) say non-protected animals, and game animals killed during open season, may be kept without a permit. Verify with ADCNR.

game_mammals: A big game animal killed or injured by a vehicle is the property of the state. In practice, Alaska Wildlife Troopers and DPS dispatch give road-killed moose (and other big game) to registered salvage teams or charities on a rotating list. The driver has no automatic right to keep the animal.
game_birds: No roadkill-specific provision found for grouse or ptarmigan. Migratory birds (waterfowl, cranes and others) are federally protected under the MBTA and cannot be possessed without a federal permit.
permit_process: The driver must notify Alaska State Troopers or Alaska Wildlife Troopers (DPS) as soon as possible. Salvage teams (2 or more people, each 18+, living in the area) apply through the DPS/AWT online roadkill program. When called, a team must accept immediately and arrive within about 30 minutes.
timing: Notify troopers as soon as possible after the collision. In Anchorage and Mat-Su, salvagers must submit a 5-inch lower jaw section and the antlers to ADF&G within 14 days. DPS may require annual reapplication.
excluded_species: No species list published. The program addresses moose; other big game is handled at trooper discretion.
sale_of_parts: Prohibited. Meat is for personal use only; it may not be sold or used as animal feed or bait.
other_restrictions: The entire animal and all remains must be removed from the scene; incomplete removal can lead to a citation and removal from the program. Edible meat must be salvaged for human consumption.
statute_or_reg: 5 AAC 92.220(b) (big game killed or injured by a vehicle is state property; driver must notify); 5 AAC 92.210 (game as animal food or bait)
agency: Alaska Department of Public Safety, Alaska Wildlife Troopers (with ADF&G)
notes: Salvage is allocated by troopers from a charity or salvage-team list, not by the driver claiming the animal. Eligible areas include Anchorage, Mat-Su, Kenai, Fairbanks, Juneau, Prince of Wales, Ketchikan and the Interior road system; other communities should contact the local AWT post.

game_mammals: Any big game animal (in Arizona: deer, elk, pronghorn, bighorn sheep, bison, javelina, black bear, mountain lion and turkey) killed in a vehicle collision, or euthanized after one, may be possessed and transported only under a big game salvage permit. Since 2021, a permit can also be issued for big game that died of natural causes.
game_birds: Wild turkey is big game in Arizona, so the big game salvage permit covers it. The statute does not cover small game or upland birds (quail, grouse, pheasant). Migratory birds are covered by the MBTA and need a federal permit.
permit_process: A peace officer or authorized AZGFD employee issues a big game salvage permit to the driver or to another person who wants the carcass. The officer completes the form, gives the original to the recipient and sends a copy to AZGFD within 48 hours. The permit is free and non-transferable.
timing: Must have the permit before possessing or transporting the carcass. The issuing officer forwards a copy to AZGFD within 48 hours. No seasonal limit.
excluded_species: Non-big-game species are not covered. No permit may be issued if the animal is suspected to be diseased or spoiled.
sale_of_parts: The permit holder may gift the carcass or parts. Sale is not authorized by 17-319, and Arizona's general prohibitions on selling wildlife apply.
other_restrictions: The permit does not certify the meat as edible, and the issuing officer, agency and AZGFD are not liable. Possessing a carcass under a fraudulently obtained permit is a class 1 misdemeanor.
notes: HB 2038 (2021, Laws 2021 ch. 128) broadened eligibility to anyone wishing to possess the carcass and to natural-cause deaths, removed the 20-day post-permit inspection provision, and added the disease/spoilage bar. The big game species list comes from general Arizona law, not from 17-319 itself.

game_mammals: Deer and bear injured or killed by incidental contact (such as a vehicle accident) must be reported to the AGFC Radio Room, and an official salvage tag number must be obtained before the animal or any part of it is possessed. A salvaged deer does not count toward the season bag limit, according to secondary sources.
game_birds: Adult gobblers (wild turkey) are expressly covered by the same report-and-salvage-tag rule. No roadkill provision found for other upland birds. Migratory birds are covered by the MBTA and need a federal permit.
permit_process: Call the AGFC Radio Room at 800-482-9262 to report the animal and receive an official salvage tag number.
timing: The salvage tag number must be obtained before possessing the animal or any part, starting at the point of initial contact. No seasonal limit stated.
excluded_species: The rule names only deer, adult gobblers and bear. Possession of other species is not addressed. Elk are big game in Arkansas but are not named in the vehicle-accident subsection. Endangered species are protected (Code 05.27).
sale_of_parts: Not authorized; general AGFC prohibitions on selling game apply.
other_restrictions: AGFC CWD Management Zone carcass-movement restrictions apply. Secondary sources say antlers may not be removed unless the deer has been tagged and checked.
statute_or_reg: AGFC Code 05.18(E), Big Game Checking Requirements (Ark. Code R. 002.01.22-032)
notes: This rule was announced as new in the 2023-24 hunting guidebook. Earlier secondary sources describing Arkansas as having 'no restrictions' are outdated.

game_mammals: Collecting, possessing or transporting road-killed deer, elk, pronghorn or wild pig is not allowed. SB 395 (2019) added Fish & Game Code § 2000.6, authorizing a Fish and Game Commission pilot wildlife salvage permit program for those species via a web portal, but the program was never established.
game_birds: No salvage allowed. Migratory birds are covered by the MBTA and need a federal permit. The pilot would not have covered birds.
permit_process: None available. The planned web-based salvage permit was never implemented.
excluded_species: All species. Even the never-implemented pilot was limited to deer, elk, pronghorn and wild pig, and excluded protected species.
other_restrictions: Under Fish & Game Code § 2000.5, only authorized state or local agencies may remove animals accidentally killed on roadways.
statute_or_reg: Cal. Fish & Game Code §§ 2000.5, 2000.6 (SB 395, Stats. 2019, ch. 869)
agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife / Fish and Game Commission
notes: Fish and Game Commission staff summary for the Oct 13-16, 2026 meeting (Item 15) recommended no action on a public request to create the pilot. Staff said the § 2000.6 rulemaking authority expired because the program was not established by the Jan 1, 2022 deadline and no funding was appropriated. SB 1163 (2024), which would have removed that deadline, died in committee. Some secondary sites wrongly describe California as 'legal with permit'.

game_mammals: Edible portions of road-killed wildlife (deer, elk, moose, pronghorn and others) may be possessed with one of: a prior letter of authorization from CPW, a valid scientific collecting permit for the species, or a donation certificate or tag issued by CPW or an authorized entity. Taking only part of the carcass (for example a backstrap) is allowed if reported.
game_birds: Wild turkey and upland birds are not expressly excluded, so they appear possessable with a CPW donation certificate. Species covered by the federal MBTA (waterfowl, doves, cranes) are excluded by the rule.
permit_process: Notify CPW (nearest field office) or another authorized agency to obtain a free donation certificate. CPW may require the animal to be presented for inspection. Beneficial-use letters of authorization are issued by the Director.
timing: Notify CPW within 48 hours of taking possession. Secondary reporting says the office visit to obtain the certificate follows within a reasonable time.
excluded_species: MBTA species; federal or state threatened or endangered species; species whose possession is otherwise prohibited by statute or regulation. Raptors and eagles are excluded through the MBTA and the federal eagle act.
sale_of_parts: Not authorized by the rule; general prohibitions on selling wildlife apply. CPW may charge the donee actual processing costs for processed meat.
other_restrictions: CPW advises not approaching or dispatching an injured animal. Colorado CWD carcass handling rules apply.
notes: Regulation text verified current through the CO Register of June 10, 2025. Bear and mountain lion are not expressly excluded by #016, but other big game possession rules may apply; confirm with CPW.

game_mammals: Deer, moose or black bear killed or seriously wounded in a motor vehicle collision may become the property of the vehicle operator, or of any other person if the operator declines. Local police, state police or a DEEP Environmental Conservation officer must first inspect the animal and issue a copy of a wildlife kill incident report.
game_birds: The statute covers only deer, moose and black bear. No provision found for turkey or upland birds, so possession is not authorized. Migratory birds are covered by the MBTA and need a federal permit.
permit_process: Call local police, state police or DEEP EnCon Police. The officer inspects the animal and issues a Wildlife Kill Incident Report, and the possessor keeps a copy.
timing: Inspection and report are required before taking possession. No seasonal limit.
excluded_species: All species other than deer, moose and black bear.
sale_of_parts: Not addressed by § 26-86; general prohibitions on selling game apply.
other_restrictions: The vehicle operator has first right to the animal.
statute_or_reg: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 26-86; see also § 26-82(a) (no violation when a deer is struck by a motor vehicle)
agency: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP), Wildlife Division / EnCon Police
notes: A 2006 amendment added moose and black bear and renamed the deer kill report the 'wildlife kill incident report'.

game_mammals: Deer only. Possessing a deer killed in a vehicle accident is illegal unless an officer has examined and tagged it with a vehicle-killed deer tag. The Nevada Legislative Counsel Bureau memo describes the statute as allowing possession during and after the deer's open season once the collision is shown to State Police or wildlife agents.
game_birds: No roadkill provision found for turkey or upland birds, so possession is not authorized. Migratory birds are covered by the MBTA and need a federal permit.
permit_process: Call DNREC Division of Fish & Wildlife Natural Resources Police (302-739-4580) or State Police. An officer examines the deer and issues a vehicle-killed deer tag.
timing: The tag is required before possession. No specific hour deadline found.
sale_of_parts: Delaware generally prohibits selling deer or deer parts (only hides of lawfully killed and checked deer may be sold).
other_restrictions: The deer must be examined and tagged by an officer.
statute_or_reg: 7 Del. C. § 794 (as cited by the Nevada LCB memo; not independently verified)
agency: Delaware DNREC Division of Fish & Wildlife (Natural Resources Police); Delaware State Police
notes: The tag requirement comes from a 2016 Delaware State Police notice. The statute citation comes from a Nov 2024 Nevada LCB research memo; I could not open the Delaware Code site to confirm the section number or text.

game_mammals: Deer only. The general ban on possessing carcasses of wildlife does not apply to a deer carcass or parts from a deer killed by accidental collision with a vehicle. No permit or report is required by the rule. Possession of other road-killed wildlife carcasses remains prohibited.
game_birds: Not covered. Wild turkey and other game bird roadkill may not be possessed. Migratory birds are covered by the MBTA and need a federal permit.
permit_process: None required for deer under the rule.
timing: No deadline or seasonal limit for deer.
excluded_species: All species other than deer, including black bear, Florida panther, Key deer (federally endangered), turkey, furbearers and protected species.
sale_of_parts: Not authorized; general FWC prohibitions on selling wildlife apply.
other_restrictions: Report vehicle-killed bears and panthers to FWC; possession is not allowed.
agency: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC)
notes: Subsection (4) was adopted effective July 1, 2010; last amended 7-29-15; text verified current through June 2025. Some secondary sites (for example LegalClarity) wrongly say Florida bans all roadkill salvage. Key deer exclusion is my inference from federal ESA protection; it is not stated in the rule.

game_mammals: Any person may lawfully possess native wildlife accidentally killed by a motor vehicle, including deer. A person who takes a bear must notify DNR or a law enforcement officer (location, name and address).
game_birds: Native game birds such as turkey and quail fall under the general native-wildlife allowance. Migratory birds (waterfowl, doves) cannot be possessed without a federal permit under the MBTA, and the statute excludes federally protected species.
permit_process: No permit for most species. For bears, report to the Georgia DNR Wildlife Resources Division or any law enforcement officer, who forwards the report to DNR within 48 hours.
timing: Bear reports are due within 48 hours of taking possession. No seasonal restriction.
excluded_species: Species protected under O.C.G.A. Title 27, Ch. 3, Art. 5 (state protected species) or federal law, including endangered species and MBTA birds such as raptors.
sale_of_parts: Not authorized by § 27-3-28; Georgia's general restrictions on selling wildlife apply.
other_restrictions: Georgia DNR CWD carcass import rules apply to deer from outside the state.
agency: Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife Resources Division
notes: Enacted 2010 (SB 474); text verified in the 2025 Code of Georgia.
